messages.author: 0d5b7d74dea6b6ad
messages.subject: Obtaining complete output
parts:
Good evening! I have a quick question about obtaining my complete output.  I am running a fairly complicated model (looking at moderation, direct, and indirect effects and checking group difference for three groups).  When my output is shown, I can only see the complete output for Groups 2 and 3. I cannot view much of Group 1's information and I cannot view my model fit. 
Might someone be able to assist me in obtaining the output I cannot see?
Thanks in advance!
Sara

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining complete output
parts:
So you just have that many parameters that your Console runs out of space?  :-)  You can change your GUI preferences. Open R (base R, not RStudio) and click on Edit --> GUI Preferences and look for the box that says "lines" to increase the number.  If you are in RStudio, there is no way to get around the 1000-line limit they use.

But it might just be easier to use the inspect() function to look at the pieces of output you are interested in.  For example:

fit <- sem(...)
inspect(fit, "fit")
myEstimates <- parameterEstimates(fit)
myEstimates
myEstimates[myEstimates$op == "=~", ]
myEstimates[myEstimates$op == "~", ]
myEstimates[myEstimates$group == 1, ]


Check out this page on the lavaan site:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/inspect.html

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining complete output
parts:
On 03/21/2015 11:41 PM, Sara wrote:
> Might someone be able to assist me in obtaining the output I cannot see?

You can use sink() to divert the output of summary() (or any other R
function) to a file. For example, in R:

sink("c:/tmp/myHugeOutput.txt") # open connection to a file
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE) # you will not see anything on the screen
sink() # close connection

and you will find all output in the file 'c:/tmp/myHugeOutput.txt'

Yves.
